summary:
The name of this bill is the Nepal Rastra Bank (Third Amendment) Act, 2083 (Section 1, Subsection 1, Page 6). This Act has been introduced to make provisions regarding the establishment of Nepal Rastra Bank as the central bank to strengthen overall financial sector stability by maintaining price and balance of payments stability with the objective of supporting the sustainable development of Nepal's economy, and to make provisions clear, systematic, and timely regarding the bank's objectives, appointment and removal of the governor and directors, financial stability mechanisms, digital currency, and regulatory authority (Objective and Reason, Page 1). This Act shall come into force immediately (Section 1, Subsection 2, Page 6).

Nepal Rastra Bank may perform functions related to quasi-fiscal operations and guarantee liabilities of the Government of Nepal, government-owned institutions, public bodies, companies, or other institutions (Section 6, Page 11). The Bank may open offices in the Kathmandu Valley and at any place within or outside Nepal (Section 3, Page 8). The Government of Nepal, Provincial Governments, Local Levels, public bodies, cooperatives, and industries/businesses are included in various provisions of this Act (Section 7, Page 13; Section 9, Page 14; Section 65, Page 56). If the Bank's audited paid-up capital decreases, the Board of Directors shall request the Government of Nepal, and the Government of Nepal shall provide the amount in cash or through negotiable debt instruments issued at prevailing interest rates within 90 days from the date of completion of the fiscal year (Section 26, Page 27-28). If the Bank's capital decreases due to revaluation loss or net loss, the Government of Nepal shall restore such capital within six months (Section 28, Page 32-33). The overdraft provided by the Bank to the Government of Nepal or entities fully, majority, or partially owned by the Government of Nepal shall not exceed 5 percent of the Government of Nepal's revenue income of the previous fiscal year at any time (Section 41, Page 38). The Government of Nepal shall repay such overdraft within 180 days in cash or through marketable debt instruments at prevailing market interest rates, and the maturity period of such marketable debt instruments shall not exceed 180 days (Section 41, Page 39). The maximum amount of debt instruments purchased by the Bank at primary issuance shall not exceed 5 percent of the average revenue income of the previous three fiscal years (Section 41, Page 39). During the resolution process, the Government of Nepal may make investments in commercial banks, financial institutions, or bridge institutions upon the recommendation of the Bank, and must recover its investment by selling it to the private sector through bidding within up to five years from the date of improvement (Section 56, Page 50-51).

Entities covered under this Act include 'A' class licensed commercial banks, financial institutions including digital banks, financial holding companies, remittance businesses, payment system operators, payment service providers, and entities carrying out financial transactions established under law whether collecting deposits or not (Section 2, Page 6-7; Section 42, Page 40). Institutions carrying out financial transactions have a duty to comply with rules, regulations, orders, directives, and notices issued by the Bank (Section 42, Page 40). If a commercial bank or financial institution is in a state of insolvency or liquidation, or is unable to pay due amounts, or is materially unable to perform obligations, it must immediately inform the Bank (Section 44, Page 41). A commercial bank or financial institution in financial crisis must get a work plan approved by its board of directors and submit it periodically to the Bank (Section 44, Page 41-42). Commercial banks or financial institutions must maintain integrated customer identification, records regarding money laundering and terrorist financing lists, and integrated details including high-ranking officials (Section 52, Page 47). Service providers providing electricity, water, telephone, data, information technology, payment and settlement, real estate, and vehicles to an institution under resolution shall not stop services solely due to resolution or outstanding dues (Section 60, Page 52-53). Any aggrieved party claiming that resolution yields lower benefits than liquidation may apply to court for monetary compensation within 60 days from the date the special administration group submits its report to the Bank or is dissolved (Section 61, Page 53-54).

The Board of Directors formulates necessary policies regarding issuing and revoking licenses for commercial banks ('A' class banks licensed under federal law) and financial institutions including digital banks, remittance entities, payment system operators, and payment service providers (Section 2, Page 6-7; Section 20, Page 20). Regarding quality standards and exchange provisions, the Bank may refuse to exchange bank notes, digital currency, or counterfeit currency if the design is erased, defaced, or does not have more than 50 percent of its portion remaining (Section 37, Page 36). The Bank shall not re-issue or put into circulation torn, defaced, worn out, or prohibited bank notes or digital currency (Section 33, Page 35). Provisions regarding printing bank notes, issuing digital currency, minting coins, destroying notes and digital currency, and security shall be as prescribed (Section 35, Page 35-36).

This bill amends provisions regarding Nepal Rastra Bank, whose main objectives are to maintain price stability and, without prejudice to price stability, maintain stability of the financial, monetary, and external sectors, while supporting the implementation of economic policies of the Government of Nepal (Section 4, Page 8-9).
